explanation: 该论文主要关注社会基础设施与紧凑型居住的关系，探讨如何通过减少私人住宅空间来降低物质和能源需求，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）无关。
authors: Tamar Meshulam;Shoshanna Saxe
title: Between public space and private living: social infrastructure as a demand-side strategy for compact living
abstract: Cities must balance the housing needs of growing populations with planetary boundaries. Technological improvements alone cannot meet climate targets, and demand-side strategies that reduce private dwelling size are critical for achieving absolute reductions in material and energy demand. However, the socio-spatial conditions that enable compact living remain poorly understood. Prior theoretical work suggests that social infrastructure, including cafés, parks, libraries, and community centres, can reduce demand for private residential space, but empirical evidence linking social infrastructure to dwelling size has been virtually absent. We address this gap through a large-scale, neighbourhood-level analysis across Vancouver, Toronto, and Montréal, Canada. Using Google Places data linked with census indicators, we estimated spatial error models to examine the association between social infrastructure and dwelling size. Across all three cities, greater access to social infrastructure was associated with smaller dwellings, independent of income, household size, and population density (β = − 0.210 Toronto; −0.138 Vancouver; −0.091 Montréal). To account for differences in urban form, we further clustered neighbourhoods into built-form typologies, enabling comparisons among similar neighbourhoods. The relationship remained significant across most typologies within each city. While further analysis is needed across additional countries and settlement types, these findings provide the first cross-metropolitan quantitative evidence linking social infrastructure with compact living. Together, these findings identify social infrastructure as a promising and previously overlooked demand-side strategy deserving greater attention in efforts to enable resource-efficient housing while maintaining urban liveability.

explanation: 该论文主要研究的是太阳能放牧系统中的有益昆虫，虽然涉及农业和生态系统，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。
authors: Leana Zoller;Nikola Kochendoerfer;Antonio DiTommaso;John Losey;Scott H McArt;Paige A Muñiz;Todd Ugine;Steven M Grodsky
title: Low solar grazing densities support beneficial insects in agrivoltaic systems
abstract: Solar grazing—the co-location of livestock grazing and photovoltaic energy production—is rapidly expanding globally to mitigate land-use conflicts. Solar facilities are increasingly sited on agricultural land, where both sheep grazing and the promotion of agriculturally beneficial insects are recognized as facilitators of multi-functional agroecosystems, yet how stocking rate shapes beneficial insect communities remains poorly understood. We conducted a replicated, three-year experiment testing six stocking rates (0–10 sheep ha−1) at an operational 18 MW solar facility, sampling bees and lady beetles across three years and four grazing rotations per year. Light grazing at 2 sheep ha−1 supported 38% greater beneficial insect abundance than ungrazed controls, driven primarily by an 83% increase in honey bees. High stocking rates (⩾8 sheep ha−1) reduced bee abundance by 42%–68% and significantly changed insect community composition. A companion study identified 8 sheep ha−1 as the agrotechnological optimum, but our results identify 2 sheep ha−1 as the agroecological optimum in our study region, where beneficial insect abundance and flock health are maximized. These optima did not coincide, indicating a clear tradeoff between ecological and operational objectives. However, at 4 sheep ha−1, beneficial insect communities remained statistically indistinguishable from ungrazed controls while vegetation management effectiveness was greater than at 2 sheep ha−1. Together these results define a synergy–tradeoff boundary with direct implications for targeting agroecological outcomes via the operations and maintenance of solar grazing facilities.

explanation: 该论文研究了西欧和长江中下游流域在2025年夏季发生的同步极端高温事件，探讨了其背后的动力学机制，涉及大气环流和Rossby波等大气环境遥感技术相关的研究内容。
authors: Wangchu Zhou;Yao Yao;Danqing Huang
title: Synchronized heat extremes over western Europe and the Yangtze–Huai River Basin during summer 2025
abstract: Western Europe and the Yangtze–Huai River Basin (YHRB) experienced two exceptional synchronized extreme heat events during the summer of 2025, providing a unique opportunity to investigate the mechanisms linking geographically distant heat extremes. Because the two events exhibit similar large-scale dynamical evolution, the first event is examined in detail to illustrate the underlying processes. Linear Baroclinic Model experiments reveal that the associated Rossby wave train is triggered by thermal anomalies whose dominant forcing migrates progressively eastward from western North America to western Asia. The synchronized extreme heat events in western Europe and YHRB are stronger, broader, and more persistent, which are mainly produced by strong, large and persistent anticyclonic anomalies of Rossby wave trains due to weaker mean upper-level potential vorticity gradients and enhanced upstream westerlies. These findings provide new insights into the development and persistence of synchronized heat extremes, with potential implications for their sub-seasonal prediction.

explanation: 该论文研究了大气中有机气溶胶的分子组成与活性氧（ROS）形成之间的关系，涉及空气质量监测、大气成分分析等技术，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Fobang Liu;Yun Zhang;Siyao Yue;Helmi-Marja K. Keskinen;Tuukka Petäjä;Markku Kulmala;Pingqing Fu;Thorsten Hoffmann;Kai Wang;Haijie Tong
title: Linking molecular composition of organic aerosols to reactive oxygen species formation using an MCR-VK framework
abstract:
Reactive oxygen species (ROS) produced by airborne particles are linked to adverse health effects, but the organic compounds responsible remain unclear. We developed a new molecular framework to classify complex organic compounds using advanced mass spectrometry. The framework shows that particles rich in oxidized organic compounds produce more ROS per unit mass, while polluted urban air produces more total ROS mainly because of higher particle concentrations. 
 Reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation by atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM) is widely implicated in adverse health effects, yet the molecular determinants of particle-level ROS formation remain poorly constrained, largely due to the chemical complexity of organic aerosol (OA). Here, we link ROS formation to molecular-level OA composition by applying a maximum carbonyl ratio-Van Krevelen framework to ambient fine PM collected from four Chinese megacities, a German semi-urban site, a boreal forest, and laboratory-generated secondary organic aerosol (SOA) from multiple precursors. Using ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry combined with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and radical measurements, we show the intrinsic ROS (H2O2 + radicals) formation potential of fine PM is governed by OA composition rather than particle mass. Volume-normalized ROS yields increase with fine PM mass concentration and dominate overall exposure in polluted urban environments. In contrast, mass-normalized ROS yields vary independently of particle loading and are strongly driven by the balance between relative fractions of oxidized organic compounds (RFOOC) and unsaturated organic compounds (RFUOC), i.e., RFOOC / RFUOC. Across urban sites, mass-normalized ROS and H2O2 yields exhibit strong correlations with RFOOC / RFUOC, establishing this metric as a robust predictor of ROS formation. Remote, biogenic-influenced aerosols exhibit higher RFOOC / RFUOC and higher ROS yields per unit mass, whereas urban aerosols exhibit the opposite behavior. Laboratory SOA further supports these composition-reactivity relationships, with OOC-rich biogenic SOA exhibiting the highest ROS yields. This study reveals molecular-level characteristics in governing aerosol ROS formation and introduces a framework for assessing health-relevant aerosol oxidative activity of chemically complex OA.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为标题和摘要中都明确提到了“Multi-angle Imaging SpectroRadiometer (MISR)”（多角度成像光谱辐射计）和“aerosol retrievals”（气溶胶反演）。MISR是一种用于监测大气成分和空气质量的卫星传感器，而气溶胶反演是大气环境遥感技术中的一个重要应用，用于分析大气中的气溶胶分布和性质。
authors: Michael Anstett;James A. Limbacher;Ralph A. Kahn
title: The MISR Research Product Algorithm – producing global, self-consistent, pixel-level aerosol retrievals for the Multi-angle Imaging SpectroRadiometer
abstract:
This paper describes the Multi-angle Imaging SpectroRadiometer (MISR) Research Product Algorithm (MRPA) and analyzes its performance. The MRPA an aerosol retrieval algorithm based on the MISR aerosol Research Algorithm (RA), which explored and introduced innovations into MISR aerosol retrievals. Previously, the RA ran on a limited, case-by-case basis. The MRPA is an automated version optimized so users can create 1.1 km-resolution, quality aerosol-type results for most of the MISR data record. 
 The MISR Research Aerosol retrieval algorithm (RA) was developed in parallel with the MISR standard operational algorithm (SA), to explore innovative retrieval ideas for possible implementation in the SA, and to provide higher-spatial-resolution results with enhanced sensitivity to particle properties, where possible.  Whereas the SA was designed to run automatically on the entire MISR dataset, the RA, a research code, had to be run on a case-by-case basis, with considerable user involvement. We present here a version of the RA, the MISR Research Product Algorithm (MRPA), that has been streamlined and automated for wider use, along with validation results for this algorithm. The compromises required to automate the RA result in somewhat diminished particle-type sensitivity. However, the MRPA provides 1.1 km pixel resolution (compared to 4.4 km for the SA), and comparing the AOD data statistically with AERONET, it offers about half the statistical RMSE, significantly higher correlation coefficient, though somewhat higher bias, for mid-visible AOD compared to the SA over land, along with better Ångström exponent statistics, especially at higher AOD. Statistical validation of particle shape and single-scattering albedo is more difficult, but for sufficiently high AOD, retrievals in smoke-dominated regions show a preponderance of small-medium, spherical, light-absorbing particles, whereas dust-dominated regions tend to have larger, weakly absorbing, non-spherical particles.

explanation: 该论文研究了使用荧光-拉曼-米散射偏振激光雷达技术从北京城市区域获取 PM2.5 垂直分布的方法。论文涉及了空气质量监测、大气成分分析和气溶胶反演等关键技术，与大气环境遥感技术高度相关。
authors: Siying Chen;Yingjie Shu;He Chen;Pan Guo;Yurong Jiang;Guoxing Hu;Xiaolei Zhang;Haokai Yang;Mengjun Feng;Yue Cao;Kaitong Zhang
title: Classification-constrained retrieval of PM2.5 vertical profiles from fluorescence-raman-mie polarization lidar
abstract:
Air pollution can change rapidly above cities, while ground monitors show conditions at only one height. We used a laser-based instrument to distinguish urban pollution particles from dust and estimate how fine-particle pollution changed with height over Beijing. Testing against independent monitoring data showed that accounting for particle type reduced errors by 38 %. This approach can improve understanding of pollution layers and their movement. 
 The vertical distribution of PM2.5 during urban haze events is jointly affected by aerosol composition, boundary-layer structure, and regional transport. Empirical PM2.5 retrievals based on lidar-derived extinction coefficients can be biased by the optical contribution of coarse-mode mineral particles. This study used fluorescence–Raman–Mie polarization lidar observations in Beijing to identify anthropogenic pollution aerosols (APA), desert dust (DD), and mineral dust (MD) using the particle depolarization ratio (PDR) and fluorescence capacity (Gf). The classification results were incorporated into the construction and application of an empirical extinction–PM2.5 relationship. For mixed-aerosol samples, the APA component fraction and its associated extinction contribution were estimated before retrieving the vertical PM2.5 distribution.To quantify the effect of classification constraints, three linear models were developed: a model without aerosol-type constraints, a PDR-only screening model, and a model constrained by combined PDR–Gf classification. Near-surface, date-separated validation using 411 hourly samples from 69 observation dates showed that the combined-classification model achieved an RMSE of 17.32 µg m−3, an MAE of 13.54 µg m−3, and a Bias of 3.30 µg m−3. Compared with the model without aerosol-type constraints, the RMSE, MAE, and Bias decreased by 38.2 %, 45.0 %, and approximately 83.0 %, respectively. Uncertainty analysis showed that classification end-member and aerosol-type-dependent lidar-ratio perturbations affected the quantitative PM2.5 estimates under mixed-aerosol conditions, whereas the residual scatter and parameter stability of the empirical extinction–PM2.5 relationship were the dominant sources of prediction uncertainty.For a mixed-to-pollution aerosol evolution episode in Beijing in November 2024, the classification-constrained PM2.5 vertical structure was physically consistent with temperature stratification, wind fields, and backward trajectories. Seasonal testing showed no stable and consistent improvement from season-specific fitting. The proposed method provides classification-constrained estimates of the PM2.5 vertical structure under APA-dominated conditions in Beijing. Model parameters should be recalibrated using local observations when applied to regions, seasons, or aerosol conditions with substantially different composition.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及使用先进的风筝仪器（MPCK+）进行机载测量，包括湍流、大气状态参数和云微物理参数，特别是在北极边界层云的研究中，这对于空气质量监测和大气成分分析等领域具有重要价值。
authors: Oliver Schlenczek;Freja Nordsiek;Claudia E. Brunner;Venecia Chávez-Medina;Birte Thiede;Eberhard Bodenschatz;Gholamhossein Bagheri
title: Airborne measurements of turbulence and cloud microphysics during PaCE 2022 using the Advanced Max Planck CloudKite Instrument (MPCK+)
abstract:
During the Pallas Cloud Experiment (PaCE) in Finland (19–26 September 2022), the Advanced Max Planck CloudKite instrument (MPCK+) gathered turbulence, atmospheric-state parameters and cloud-microphysics from 0–1200 m. Flights lasted 1.5–3 hours, capturing droplet concentrations and size distributions at high resolution (<10 m spacing). The dataset aids studies of Arctic boundary layer clouds above freezing temperatures. This paper details the data collection, structure, and user guidelines. 
 This paper presents the data set collected with the Advanced Max Planck CloudKite instrument (MPCK+) during the Pallas Cloud Experiment (PaCE), conducted at Pallas, Finland, between  19 and 26 September 2022. The data set includes measurements of turbulence, wind shear, and cloud microphysics in the cloudy planetary boundary layer between 0 and 1200 m above ground with flight durations between 1.5 and 3 h. This data set is intended for researchers studying microphysics of boundary layer clouds in the sub-arctic at temperatures above freezing level, providing high-resolution airborne measurements of meteorological variables together with cloud droplet concentration and size distribution data. In particular, the high spatial resolution of less than 10 m between two cloud droplet size distribution samples, the low altitude and the long flight time allow unprecedented insights into stratocumulus and cumulus clouds. The aim of this paper is to describe the data collection process, the structure of the data set, and guidelines for potential users. The data set is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15700506 (Bagheri et al., 2025a) in NetCDF format.

explanation: 该论文主要研究美国境内快速发生的洪水现象，涉及洪水报告、降雨、河流流量等数据，虽然与大气环境有一定关联（如降雨数据），但核心内容并非大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等。
authors: Songkun Yan;Mengye Chen;Jonathan J. Gourley;Jian Zhang;Günter Blöschl;Paul Bates;Zhi Li;Siyu Zhu;Abigail Snooks;Yixin Wen;Xiaodong Chen;Chengbin Deng;Juan Camilo Parra Toro;Meihong Ma;Yang Hong
title: TORRENT: An observation-constrained and benchmark-ready community shared dataset in the contiguous United States for flash-flood research and model intercomparison
abstract:
Flash floods develop quickly, but the records needed to study them are scattered across many sources. We created TORRENT by linking flood reports, rainfall, river flow, drainage-area information, and field measurements across the contiguous United States. It contains 42 466 reported events and 806 ready-to-use case packages, including 21 carefully checked cases. Its open, machine-readable design will help people and artificial intelligence tools study floods and compare prediction methods. 
 Flash floods develop within minutes to hours, occur mainly in small to medium-sized watersheds, and are documented through scattered sources such as news reports, social media, stream gauges, operational storm events databases, and post-flood field surveys. Such fragmentation historically limits flash flood research advances and model evaluation or intercomparisons. We present TORRENT (the Traceable, Observation-constrained, Rapid-Response, Episode–gauge–watershed Network of Testbeds), a benchmark-ready community dataset of flash-flood hydrological response in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Each testbed links one reported NOAA/NCEI flash-flood episode, one U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) stream gauge, and the gauge’s contributing watershed, combining the observed discharge hydrograph—the primary benchmark target—with watershed boundaries, temporally screened in-basin high-water marks, and quality-control metadata; full packages additionally provide Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor (MRMS) precipitation forcing and auxiliary gridded products. TORRENT follows a three-level structure distinguishing what was reported, what observations are available, and what can be evaluated reproducibly: a national inventory of 42,466 reported episodes for 1996–2025; observation-availability documentation for 5,424 recent CONUS episodes during 2021–2025, including episodes without usable external observations; and 806 episode–gauge–watershed evaluation packages representing 160 episodes and 208 gauges. Each Level-3 package has a retrievable watershed, at least one in-basin high-water mark meeting the stated temporal-screening criterion, and a detected discharge response. Flash-flood-response screening, deduplication, in-basin NCEI corroboration, station-relative severity screening, and post-selection curation yield a conservative primary benchmark of 21 testbeds representing 14 episodes and 21 gauges. This primary set is intended as a high-confidence reference for formal rainfall–runoff model intercomparison rather than as a statistically representative sample of CONUS flash floods; the broader Level-3 pool supports exploratory analysis and robustness testing. Primary testbeds exhibit rapid, pronounced responses, with estimated event-peak return periods ranging from about 2 to more than 100 years. The automated construction and screening stages are released as deterministic, re-runnable code, together with documented curation decisions, sensitivity tests, and quality-control diagnostics. TORRENT is openly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23359069 (Yan et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究跨大西洋气溶胶传输，特别是来自北非的矿物尘，这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及使用多种仪器对近地表和悬浮气溶胶进行观测，并填补了热带大西洋地区观测数据的空白。
authors: Andebo Waza;Konrad Kandler;Franz Kanngießer;Julia Gottschall;Arne Leuzinger;Simon Speith;Natalia Sudarchikova;Sebastian Wahl;Wirginia Hepert;Stephanie Fiedler
title: Trans-Atlantic aerosol transport from January to March 2025 – measurements from two expeditions on a research vessel
abstract:
Originating from North Africa, mineral dust, which is one of the most abundant aerosol types in the Earth’s atmosphere, is frequently transported across the Atlantic Ocean. To observe these dust transport different instruments, which provide information on both near-surface dust and lofted dust plumes, were deployed during two research cruises between January and March 2025 in the Atlantic Ocean. The presented data allows us to address existing knowledge gaps in trans-Atlantic dust transport. 
 Saharan dust outbreaks frequently propagate over the tropical Atlantic, but only few in-situ and ground-based remote sensing observations exist over the region. Here, we document data from EXperiments with the Portable Observatory for aeRosol Transport ("EXPORT") conducted during the expeditions M207 and M208 aboard the German research vessel R/V METEOR. The expedition M207 commenced on January 3, 2025, departing from Belém, Brazil, and concluded in Mindelo, Cabo Verde, on February 11, 2025. Expedition M208 both started and ended in Mindelo, Cabo Verde and lasted from February 15, 2025 until March, 17 2025. Throughout the expeditions, continuous measurements of aerosols and meteorological conditions were carried out. The data collection covers three distinct several-day long Saharan dust events, with the first plume over the tropical mid-Atlantic and the latter two dust plumes closer to the African continent.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它涉及使用ERA5数据集构建全球极端天气事件（如热浪、寒潮、强降水和极端风）的气候数据集（TailWeather），用于机器学习天气预报的测试和评估。这些极端天气事件对空气质量监测和大气成分分析有重要影响，因此该研究对大气环境遥感技术具有高度相关性。
authors: Zhi-Song Liu;Michael Boy;Risto Makkonen
title: TailWeather: from tail to extremes, a global climatological dataset for machine-learning weather forecasting
abstract:
Weather forecasts are mostly judged on ordinary days, not on the rare heatwaves, cold spells, storms, downpours, and droughts that cause most harm. We built a global daily record of such unusual weather over land since 1981 and compared it with reported disasters. Rarer weather was more often linked to harm, but disaster records miss much of the world. Leading artificial intelligence forecasts often missed extremes, especially strong winds, so forecasts need testing on extremes everywhere. 
 Weather forecasting models are usually judged by their average skill, yet average skill says little about the rare conditions that matter most. Testing forecasts on those conditions requires a target defined consistently everywhere. Disaster catalogs record harm, but they are sparse and shaped by reporting; climatological tails can be defined everywhere, but rarity does not imply harm. We present TailWeather, a global, land-only, 0.25° dataset of climatological tail events derived from ERA5, covering 1981–2022 and early January 2023. It labels heatwaves, cold waves, heavy precipitation, and extreme wind daily, and meteorological drought monthly. Every label carries an ordinal severity tier and an intensity score relative to the local 1991–2020 climate, so users can move thresholds, within the score’s resolution, without recomputing the climatology. Compared with the EM-DAT disaster catalog, stricter tails are more strongly enriched in recorded impacts for all five hazards, by 1.6 (extreme wind) to 9.3 times (heatwave) at the best-balanced threshold. Yet 80.1 % of the world’s land population lives where the catalog is too sparse to test this link locally for at least one hazard. In forecast examples, leading AI systems that predict 2 m temperature to within about 1 K at day 1 reach a critical success index below 0.5 on heatwave tails, and their tail skill is lowest for extreme wind. TailWeather offers a reusable physical target for studying and evaluating weather extremes, one that complements rather than replaces disaster catalogs. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/10661.

explanation: 该论文研究了水稳定同位素在大气模型中的应用，涉及大气过程和同位素分馏，与大气环境遥感技术中的成分分析和气溶胶反演等方向相关。
authors: Christelle Barthe;Françoise Vimeux;Camille Risi;Sören François
title: Meso-NH-ISO v1.0: a water stable isotopologue scheme in the non-hydrostatic mesoscale atmospheric model Meso-NH – application to a 2D West African squall line
abstract:
We implemented water stable isotopologues in the non-hydrostatic mesoscale atmospheric model Meso-NH. We validated this isotopic version (Meso-NH-ISO) with a simulation of a well-documented squall line in the Sahel region. In future works, simulations with Meso-NH-ISO will be done on real cases of cyclones or squall lines. The goal is to better interpret and quantify isotopic observations on the field in terms of atmospheric processes that drive development and intensity of those thunderstorms. 
 Better understanding how convective processes impact the isotopic composition of atmospheric water has implications for understanding phenomena such as squall lines or tropical cyclones, and for reconstructions of past rainfall extreme events. With this motivation, we implemented water stable isotopologues (HD16O and H218O) in the non-hydrostatic mesoscale atmospheric model Meso-NH and its one-moment bulk mixed-phase microphysics scheme. The water stable isotopologues are subject to the same dynamical and physical processes as the light water, but undergo isotopic fractionation during water phase changes. Both equilibrium and kinetic fractionation processes that occur during water phase changes involving water vapor are taken into account. The implementation is validated on a test case of a 2D simulation of a tropical squall line observed in June 1981 during the COPT 81 field campaign in the Sahel region. The isotopic version of Meso-NH (Meso-NH-ISO) captures the expected evolution of the isotopic composition of both precipitation and water vapor along the squall line. This work opens the door to future isotopic studies using realistic cases of mesoscale convective systems (squall lines, tropical cyclones).

explanation: 该论文研究了利用卫星观测技术（Fengyun-4B Geostationary High-speed Imager）获取大气运动矢量并推导上层涡度指标（VORm），以监测台风的短期强度变化。这与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，特别是卫星观测和台风强度预测领域。
authors: Pan Xia;Difei Deng;Xia Yang;Savin S. Chand;Min Min;Jun Li;Na Xu;Deming Meng;Qiang Yu;Rundong Zhou
title: Satellite‐Derived Upper‐Level Vorticity as an Indicator of Short‐Term Typhoon Intensity Evolution
abstract: Accurate short‐term tropical cyclone (TC) intensity forecasting remains challenging because rapidly evolving inner‐core structures are difficult to observe at sufficiently high temporal resolution. Here, we derive an area‐mean upper‐level vorticity indicator (VORm) from minute‐scale atmospheric motion vectors retrieved from the Fengyun‐4B Geostationary High‐speed Imager (FY‐4B/GHI) using the Single‐Plane Assumption–Fast Approximate Barnes Interpolation framework. Analysis of western North Pacific TCs shows that VORm closely follows the broad evolution of storm intensity while retaining substantial high‐frequency structural variability. VORm exhibits a strong contemporaneous association with TC intensity and retains information related to subsequent 6‐hr intensity change after accounting for the current intensity and preceding intensity tendency, indicating potential value for short‐term intensity prediction. Forecast experiments further demonstrate this predictive potential. In the linear framework, incorporating VORm reduced the pooled 6‐hr RMSE from 6.27 to 5.97 kt, indicating additional predictive information beyond conventional intensity and environmental predictors. In the nonlinear XGBoost framework, VORm further reduced the RMSE from 6.26 to 6.18 kt even when the preceding 6‐hr intensity tendency was explicitly included, indicating that VORm still provides additional predictive information beyond recent intensity evolution. Because FY‐4B/GHI winds and the derived vorticity can be obtained with very low latency, this approach offers a practical pathway for rapidly incorporating high‐frequency inner‐core structural information into short‐range TC intensity forecasting.

explanation: 该论文主要研究的是断层阀系统的微观力学行为，涉及流体注入和断层反应，但不直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等。
authors: Oussama Larkem;Luc Scholtès;Fabrice Golfier
title: Micromechanical Insights Into the Cyclic Behavior of Fault‐Valve Systems
abstract: Cyclic fluid pressurization can promote repeated fault reactivation and transient permeability changes, a behavior often discussed within the fault‐valve concept in which faults alternate between acting as hydraulic barriers and conduits. To investigate the micromechanical processes involved during fluid induced reactivations, we simulate cyclic fluid injection into a pre‐sheared granular gouge using a discrete element model. The simulations reproduce key behaviors observed in laboratory and in situ studies and reveal pronounced cycle‐to‐cycle variability in the onset of reactivation and slip magnitude. Some cycles generate large slip episodes, whereas others produce comparatively small slip under similar loading conditions. Micromechanical analysis of force‐chain evolution reveals a strong inverse correlation between slip magnitude and the population of load‐bearing chains, with sparser force‐chain backbones generating larger slip events. Our results highlight the role of micromechanical processes in controlling macroscopic cyclic fault behavior, offering a physically grounded perspective on fault‐valve behavior.

explanation: 该论文研究的是地震学中的断层相互作用和地震触发机制，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）无关。
authors: Yuki Watanabe;Yuta Mitsui
title: Patch Interactions on a Heterogeneous Fault Drive Nearby Slow and Fast Earthquakes
abstract: Tectonic tremor and repeating/regular earthquakes off Iwate in the shallow Japan Trench occur episodically and in spatially overlapping areas, implying a common aseismic driver. We investigate how small aseismic slip triggers events across multiple slip‐rate regimes using fully dynamic earthquake‐cycle simulations governed by rate‐and‐state friction. Along‐fault heterogeneity is imposed by alternating velocity‐weakening (VW) and velocity‐strengthening (VS) patches, and events are classified based on peak slip velocity Vmax ${V}_{\max }$. A single VW patch produces only aseismic events, whereas a multi‐patch heterogeneous model generates sub‐seismic slip and earthquakes, often nearly synchronous across VW patches. Inter‐event transient slip in VS patches raises stress during subsequent VW nucleation. Transitions in Vmax ${V}_{\max }$ and rupture properties are controlled by subtle stress differences between nucleating VW patches and surrounding VS patches. This mechanism provides a simple physical explanation for why slow and fast earthquakes can emerge from interacting fault patches with spatial overlap and close temporal proximity.

authors: Yukina Hara;Dai Yamazaki;Megumi Watanabe;Colin J. Gleason;Shinjiro Kanae
title: Observation of Daily Flood Hazard During the SWOT Cal/Val Orbit
abstract: Flood peaks can develop and recede within a day, making them difficult to capture with satellites with multi‐day revisit intervals. Here, we exploit daily observations during the Calibration and Validation phase of the SWOT mission to examine a short‐lived flood in May 2023 along the Du Gouffre River in Canada. Despite channel widths below 100 m, SWOT tracked day‐to‐day changes in water surface elevation, capturing a rapid rise of approximately 5 m consistent in timing and magnitude with in situ measurements. We derived flood extent based on classification and confidence information. The results show partial spatial overlap with an independent post‐event flood hazard map, with differences primarily associated with reduced classification confidence in vegetated floodplains and narrow reaches. Some areas not identified as water may reflect erosion, sediment deposition, or post‐peak conditions. These results highlight the value of high‐frequency wide‐swath radar altimetry for monitoring transient floods.

explanation: 该论文研究了复合干旱热浪事件（CDHEs）对生态系统和热应激风险的影响，使用了1961年至2022年的再分析数据来描述全球夏季CDHE的生命周期。虽然论文的主要内容是生态和气候科学，但其使用了再分析数据（一种基于卫星和气象站数据的再处理技术），这与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测和大气成分分析）密切相关，因此与大气环境遥感技术有较强的相关性。
authors: Yi Yang;Jianping Tang
title: Regime Shifts During Compound Drought‐Heatwave Events Amplify Ecosystem and Heat Stress Risks
abstract: Compound drought‐heatwave events (CDHEs) can cause severe ecological and socioeconomic impacts worldwide. However, their mechanisms are often inferred from seasonal statistics or event‐mean composites that obscure within‐event process evolution. Here we develop a daily regime‐based framework to characterize global summer CDHE lifecycles using reanalysis data from 1961 to 2022. Most events remain within a single thermodynamic regime, whereas a recurrent minority undergoes within‐event regime shifts. The two leading transition pathways remain far less frequent than steady pathways, but events following them last longer, are more severe, and have increased significantly over recent decades. Sunny‐Humid to Advective transitions are linked to strengthened warm air transport and amplified human heat stress, whereas Sunny‐Humid to Sunny‐Dry transitions reflect a shift toward moisture‐limited conditions and larger declines in ecosystem productivity. Accounting for daily process evolution can therefore improve assessments of compound drought‐heatwave risks in a warming climate.

authors: Xi Wang;Wenjian Hua;Aiguo Dai;Lu Zhou;Minhua Qin;Haishan Chen
title: Multidecadal Changes in Atmospheric Dryness Over East Asia Dominated by Internal Climate Variability
abstract: Summer near‐surface vapor pressure deficit (VPD), a key measure of atmospheric dryness, has increased markedly across East Asia since 1980, yet the relative roles of external forcing and internal variability (IV) in its multidecadal changes remain unclear. Here we show that IV dominates East Asian VPD variability during 1901–2024, accounting for about 81% of the total variance and largely explaining the recent drying over northern China. We identify the Indian Ocean Basin Mode (IOBM) as a key oceanic driver of this variability. A positive IOBM phase triggers a Pacific–Japan pattern‐like teleconnection, enhances subsidence and warming over East Asia and suppresses moisture transport into northern China, thereby increasing VPD. Indian Ocean pacemaker experiments capture the main circulation and warming responses, supporting this mechanism. Together, these results provide robust evidence that tropical Indian Ocean–driven IV has played a decisive role in recent atmospheric drying over East Asia.

authors: Jidong Gao;Derek R. Stratman
title: Potential Benefits of Assimilating Phased Array Radar Data for Convective‐Scale Analysis and Prediction of Supercell Storms: A Proof‐of‐Concept OSSE Study
abstract: This study investigates the impact of phased array radar (PAR) scanning strategies on short‐term convective‐scale analyses and forecasts through an Observing System Simulation Experiment framework. The Weather Research and Forecasting model, coupled with the Data Assimilation Research Testbed ensemble adjustment Kalman filter, is used to assimilate synthetic radar observations from PAR and WSR‐88D scanning strategies across three idealized supercell cases: slow‐moving, fast‐moving, and fast‐moving/fast‐growing storms. For the slow‐moving storm, PAR and WSR‐88D experiments produce comparable analyses and forecasts, with only marginal improvement from PAR. In contrast, for fast‐moving and fast‐growing storms, the 5‐min WSR‐88D scan introduces substantial temporal errors associated with storm advection and evolution, resulting in distorted storm structure. The rapid 1‐min update capability of PAR significantly reduces these errors, producing superior analyses and forecasts. These findings suggest that the implementation of a future US national PAR network would substantially enhance the accuracy of short‐term severe weather forecasts.

authors: Yang Zheng;Kang Duan;Huiru Lei;Di Wang;Qiangyong Zhang;Dejun Liu
title: Mechanical Irreversibility and Strength Overcompensation in a Gypsum Dehydration–Rehydration Cycle
abstract: Dehydration–rehydration reactions of hydrous minerals modify rock strength, fluid transport, and deformation in reactive geological environments. Although dehydration‐induced weakening is widely studied, the mechanical consequences of subsequent rehydration remain poorly constrained. We combine triaxial compression tests with microstructural and pore‐network analyses of original gypsum, fully dehydrated anhydrite, and rehydrated gypsum. Dehydration markedly reduces strength and suppresses pronounced serrated stress drops, whereas rehydration produces strength overcompensation and a more localized strain‐softening response. Rehydration does not simply restore the original fabric but produces a reconstructed microstructure containing newly formed gypsum crystals, locally infilled voids, and a reconfigured accessible pore‐throat network. Reaction‐induced stresses may contribute to this restructuring but were not measured directly. These results show that gypsum rehydration can create a mechanically distinct, overcompensated state rather than simply reverse dehydration.

authors: Hajin Song;Jae‐Hun Park;Jeong‐Yeob Chae;Kathleen A. Donohue;D. Randolph Watts;Ahyoung Ku;Kiduk Kim;Tae‐Wan Kim;Jisoo Park
title: ENSO's Imprint on the Southern Ocean: Wind Waves Drive Surface Cross‐Frontal Flow
abstract: Tropical teleconnection associated with El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is widely recognized for regulating multiple physical processes in the Southern Ocean. However, despite its influence on Southern Ocean wind patterns, the response of surface flow has received little attention. Here, we investigate surface flow in the Southern Ocean using surface‐drifting buoy trajectories collected during September 2022–May 2023 and November 2023–June 2024. Drifter observations exhibit significant cross‐frontal movements primarily driven by Stokes drift rather than Ekman velocity. The observations also show interannual variability, with strong poleward cross‐frontal flow in 2024 during a strong El Niño event. Further analyses over the past approximately 31 years indicate that ENSO teleconnection is the primary driver of this interannual variability. These findings provide a new perspective on how tropical teleconnection influences cross‐frontal flow via wind waves and highlight their potential role in tracer transport across fronts.

authors: Satoru Okajima;Shoichiro Kido;Hiroyuki Tomita;Meghan F. Cronin
title: Rectified Effect of Synoptic‐Scale Atmospheric Eddies on Global Ocean‐Atmosphere Heat Exchanges
abstract: Midlatitude oceans are characterized by vigorous turbulent heat flux (THF) from the ocean to the atmosphere. While the influence of sub‐weekly, synoptic‐scale atmospheric eddies on short‐term THF variability is well‐documented, their long‐term, “rectified” effect on air‐sea interactions remains poorly understood. Here we present a global assessment of these synoptic‐scale eddies' effects on climatological‐mean and interannual variability of THF. We demonstrate that synoptic‐scale atmospheric fluctuations enhance annual‐mean climatological upward THF almost globally, primarily by increasing wind speed. This enhancement is maximized around midlatitude oceanic frontal zones, reaching ∼30% of the climatology. In addition, atmospheric eddies amplify interannual THF variability in mid‐ and high‐latitudes although suppressing the variability in low‐latitudes. Our findings underscore the importance of synoptic‐scale atmospheric eddies for long‐term air‐sea interactions, especially in midlatitudes, and the need to appropriately represent storm‐tracks in climate models to obtain realistic mean states.

explanation: 该论文研究浅层积云边界的分形维度，涉及云的几何复杂性和云与环境相互作用，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关。论文使用了大涡模拟和分形方法来分析云边界，这与遥感技术中用于解析大气现象的定量分析方法一致。
authors: Qiqi Song;Jingyi Chen;Martin Janssens;Chunsong Lu
title: Fractal Dimension of Shallow Cumulus Cloud Boundaries Beyond Bulk Fractal Scaling
abstract: Cloud boundaries reflect turbulent mixing and cloud–environment interactions, but their geometric complexity remains poorly quantified. Here, we investigate the complexity of shallow cumulus cloud edge using two fractal approaches: the bulk area–perimeter method and the individual‐cloud box‐counting method. Using large‐eddy simulations, we find that the box‐counting dimension better captures boundary complexity by resolving cloud‐scale irregularities, whereas the bulk dimension smooths individual morphological variability. Larger clouds exhibit higher box‐counting dimensions and increased deviations from idealized stochastic self‐similar scaling, indicating increasing boundary heterogeneity with cloud size and shape complexity. Wind induces scale‐dependent morphological responses, smoothing small clouds while enhancing boundary complexity in larger clouds through competing dynamical effects. Moreover, box‐counting dimension shows a stronger association with precipitation‐related properties, suggesting a closer link between boundary evolution and cloud processes. These results highlight individual‐cloud fractal analysis as a useful framework for quantifying shallow cumulus complexity and its environmental controls.

authors: Zachary McGraw;Benjamin O. Goldman;Lorenzo M. Polvani
title: No Evidence for Strongly Enhanced Northern Hemisphere Cooling From Extratropical Versus Tropical Eruptions
abstract: Volcanic eruptions in the Northern Hemisphere extratropics have been reported to produce several times greater cooling in that region than tropical eruptions of similar magnitude. Using a large ensemble of simulations spanning the eruption size range from 5 to 40 Tg of stratospheric sulfur, we find that the extratropical‐to‐tropical cooling ratio is consistently within a factor of two, indicating no enhancement beyond the effect of aerosols being confined to a single hemisphere. We further show that paleoclimate evidence suggests similarly unexceptional cooling, and also reconcile why earlier analyses yielded unreliable estimates. Moreover, owing to their rarity, we argue that extratropical eruptions exert a smaller overall influence on Northern Hemisphere extratropical temperatures than tropical eruptions. These findings question the notion that extratropical eruptions are of outsized importance for the climate of the Northern Hemisphere.

authors: Alex S. J. Wyatt;Timothy B. King;I‐Huan Lee;James J. Leichter
title: Coral Reef‐Level Upwelling in an Internal Wave Hotspot Modulated by Mesoscale Dynamics
abstract: Coral reefs in the northern South China Sea experience some of the world’s most energetic internal waves (IWs), yet records of how these dynamics influence reef‐level conditions are rare. Using over 6 years of temperature data from Dongsha Atoll, we show that IWs drive diel temperature fluctuations that reduce subsurface heat exposure and entrain cool, nitrate‐rich water onto the reef slope. This internal‐wave‐driven upwelling is strongly modulated by mesoscale circulation: positive sea‐level anomalies associated with Kuroshio intrusion and long‐lived anticyclonic eddies cause a two‐stage suppression of internal‐wave generation and arrival, first near the Luzon Strait and subsequently over the reef. Reduced reef‐slope internal‐wave expression lowered nitrate exposure by >100‐fold at the reef. Typhoons injected near‐inertial energy but were followed by declines in cooling and nitrate supply until restratification. These results demonstrate mesoscale and episodic processes regulating internal‐wave cooling and nutrient upwelling, revealing coupled, multi‐scale physical‐biogeochemical controls on reef resilience under ocean warming.

authors: Liying Qian;Chih‐Ting Hsu;Wenbin Wang;Shun‐Rong Zhang;Joseph McInerney
title: Long‐Term Increase in Equatorial Rayleigh‐Taylor Instability: Synergistic Effects of Greenhouse Gas Cooling and Geomagnetic Field Secular Variation
abstract: Equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) are ionospheric irregularities generated by Rayleigh–Taylor instability (RTI) that disrupt satellite communications. We quantify secular change of RTI growth rates and isolate underlying drivers using WACCM‐X simulations. Results reveal a significant increase in RTI growth rates at plasma bubble initiation altitudes, with greenhouse gas cooling as the dominant driver and geomagnetic field secular variation modulating trends by longitude. We identify reduced recombination damping, often overlooked, as a major contributor. In the American/western sector, magnetic field secular variation produces localized decreases in RTI growth rates for magnetic field lines with apex altitudes of ∼250–320 km but predominantly enhances RTI growth rates for field lines with higher apex altitudes. Note that EPBs are initiated at the bottom F2 region, regardless of apex altitudes of field lines. Overall, the equatorial ionosphere is becoming more susceptible to RTI and plasma bubble development through stronger forcing and weaker damping.

title: Spatial Structure and Lifecycle Variability of Compound Dry‐Hot and Heavy Rainfall Events Over the North China Plain
abstract: Spatially compound dry‐hot and heavy rainfall events expose neighboring areas to simultaneous water and heat hazards, but regional averages obscure how their components are arranged and evolve. This limits identification of recurrent event structures and the conditions associated with them. We developed an object‐based framework to detect and track paired dry‐hot and heavy rainfall patches over the North China Plain during May–October 1979–2025. Displacement‐based criteria classified spatial arrangement, whereas K‐means summarized lifecycle and geometry descriptors into organization regimes. Among 182 events, 121 (66.5%) were meridional dipoles, including 103 wet‐north/dry‐south cases. The organization analysis identified 87 pulse‐active and 95 persistent‐migratory events. Persistent‐migratory events lasted longer, migrated farther, and maintained stronger 850 hPa meridional moisture transport after onset (q adjusted for the false discovery rate = 0.011). Independent gridded products reproduced anomalies averaged over the domain (r = 0.695–0.953), although patch outlines agreed less closely. Temporally blocked antecedent models discriminated organization regime only weakly (balanced accuracy 0.542; Brier skill −0.407). Under fixed 1979–2010 thresholds, event frequency increased by 133.3% from 1979 to 2001 to 2002–2025. The catalog therefore reveals recurrent spatial and lifecycle structures, but event structure carries only a weak transferable antecedent signal. Its rising frequency broadens the range of configurations that regional risk management must accommodate.

title: Palaeoclimate constraints narrow uncertainty in future Arctic winter sea ice projections
abstract:
Forecasts of future Arctic Ocean sea ice loss can be substantially improved using Holocene proxy records by applying a model weighting approach. 
 Arctic sea ice decline has been observed across all seasons and is projected to continue in the future. Relative to historical observations, climate models show their largest biases and uncertainties during winter, when ice cover strongly regulates air–sea heat exchange, ocean mixing and atmospheric circulation. Palaeoclimate records offer opportunities to evaluate model performance beyond the historical period, but applications have remained largely qualitative. Here we compile an Arctic-wide database of mid-Holocene (5–7 thousand years ago) biomarkers to assess sea ice simulations of this past warm period. Using a recently developed proxy system model, we present a Bayesian palaeoclimate model weighting scheme that refines the multi-model mean winter sea ice extent through fully quantitative proxy-model comparisons, accounting for model interdependence and non-stationary proxy seasonality. We demonstrate that, by adjusting the contribution of each model to the ensemble mean based on proxy evidence, model weights can eliminate biases and reduce uncertainties by 85%, to the level of interannual variability. Weighted projections using the same climate models indicate that future winter sea ice extent may be nearly 1 million km2 lower than prior estimates across forthcoming decades and possible emissions scenarios, with broad implications for Arctic ecosystems, mid-latitude weather, and cryosphere stability. Forecasts of future Arctic Ocean sea ice loss can be substantially improved using Holocene proxy records by applying a model weighting approach.

authors: Guangqi Xiong;Zhao Meng;Yanran Cheng;Shuangshuang Liu;Yong Zheng;Chi Sun Poon;Shipeng Zhang
title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
abstract:
Ultrasound carbonation confines water distribution, creating submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials that combine low density, high specific strength, improved sound insulation and CO2 uptake without conventional foaming agents. 
 Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg−1, representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production. Ultrasound carbonation confines water distribution, creating submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials that combine low density, high specific strength, improved sound insulation and CO2 uptake without conventional foaming agents.

authors: Nathalie Casas;Guilhem Mollon;Marco Maria Scuderi
title: From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening
abstract:
This study combines simulations and laboratory data to show how grains breaking inside fault gouge reshape fault-zone architecture, focus slip into narrow bands and help faults weaken during deformation. 
 Earthquake nucleation is governed by the evolution of fault zone structure, yet the physical mechanisms linking grain-scale processes to macroscopic weakening remain elusive. Here we use discrete element simulations of quartz-rich gouge in which angular grains fragment dynamically, revealing a robust strain–damage law in which damage accumulates as grains are consumed. Grain size dictates the geometry and timing of localization, while fragmentation enhances compaction and promotes the emergence of a dominant Principal Slip Zone (PSZ). As comminution approaches a saturation state (i.e. minimum grain size), localization can migrate to competing bands, providing a mechanical explanation for overprinted shear fabrics in experiments and natural faults. By linking fragmentation, porosity evolution, and the resulting shear localization, our results provide a local fragmentation state variable for constitutive laws that couple grain-size evolution to fault weakening and the conditions for earthquake nucleation. This study combines simulations and laboratory data to show how grains breaking inside fault gouge reshape fault-zone architecture, focus slip into narrow bands and help faults weaken during deformation.

title: Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
abstract:
Temporary carbon removal and storage can lead to avoided changes in slow responding climate variables that extend beyond the duration of storage itself. These climate benefits are greater when storage is paired with ambitious climate mitigation. 
 Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation. Apelin can counteract water retention and may help correct low blood sodium. Here, the authors show in a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial that intravenous apelin does not meaningfully increase urine output in adults with experimentally induced hyponatremia.

Administration of apelin analogues increased urine output in hyponatremic rodent models, but corresponding human data are lacking. We therefore investigated intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in healthy participants with artificially induced syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis. In this double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study, 15 healthy adults (7 female; mean age, 28 years [SD, 8]) attended three study visits. title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
abstract:
Regulatory genetic variants can influence disease risk through effects on chromatin activity, but studying these effects across tissues remains challenging. Here, the authors use cell‑free chromatin profiling to identify chromatin quantitative trait loci across diverse tissues, linking regulatory variation to hundreds of human traits and diseases. 
 A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations. abstract:
Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) lacks effective local therapies. Here, the authors develop an NIR-responsive microneedle patch that locally delivers cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA), reduces pain and cartilage degeneration, and suppresses MMP-associated pathological remodeling. 
 Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. The system provides mechanical integrity, photothermal responsiveness and NIR-assisted local drug release. In a mouse TMJ-OA model, SFZICC MNs combined with NIR irradiation reduce mechanical hypersensitivity, anxiety-like behaviors, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascularization, and outperform free CCA, blank microneedles and drug-loaded microneedles without NIR. Mechanistically, CCA directly interacts with MMP3, MMP9 and MMP13 and moderately inhibits their catalytic activities in vitro, while reducing intracellular superoxide accumulation, NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and MMP protein abundance. In vivo imaging further supports reduced overall MMP-associated proteolytic activity. These findings support SFZICC MNs as a locally responsive therapeutic platform for TMJ-OA. title: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
abstract:
Continuous glucose monitoring is central to diabetes management, yet conventional testing provides only intermittent snapshots and may miss clinically important glycaemic fluctuations. Here, the authors present a wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform that combines active interstitial fluid extraction with nonenzymatic electrochemical glucose sensing in a wearable format. Its detachable microneedle cartridge enables independent cleaning or replacement, supporting quasi-continuous monitoring while improving practicality and long-term usability for wearable glucose tracking. 
 Continuous glucose monitoring in interstitial fluid (ISF) is important for diabetes management, but enzyme-based sensors can lose activity, while many nonenzymatic alternatives show optimal activity in alkaline media. Here we present a regenerable wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform for closed-loop nonenzymatic ISF glucose monitoring. Negative pressure extracts ISF into a detachable sensor cartridge that separates the tissue interface from the electrochemical sensing chamber and enables rinsing and reuse. A brief cathodic step triggers the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at an Au–Pt/Ni foam electrode, electrochemically generating a local alkaline interface for the subsequent glucose oxidation reaction (GOR). Integrated pH feedback regulates the HER–GOR sequence. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate rapid ISF extraction and quasi-continuous glucose monitoring in rats, with preliminary feasibility in one human participant. This work illustrates local microenvironment regulation as a strategy for enabling alkaline-dependent glucose electrocatalysis in near-neutral ISF. Mechanisms behind climate decision-making remain unclear. This study shows that political affiliation and subjective attribution shape attention allocation and climate-related choices, with subjective attribution moderating the effects of political affiliation and objective weather exposure. 
 Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample (N = 1,451). We combined a process-tracing paradigm within an incentivized decision task involving real carbon emissions with objective data on extreme weather exposure. Democrats attended more to carbon emission information and made more pro-climate choices than Republicans, with no evidence of moderation by objective extreme weather exposure. The subjective attribution of extreme weather to climate change was associated with greater attention to carbon information, more pro-climate choices and moderated the effects of exposure on both outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of political affiliation in climate-relevant decision-making and suggest that extreme weather effects depend less on exposure itself than on how these experiences are interpreted. abstract:
Winter monsoon variability accompanies Xisha SST–North China hydroclimate teleconnection reversal during the Medieval climate anomaly 
 Winter sea surface temperature (SST) in the South China Sea is a precursor of North China hydroclimate, but the relationship’s long-term stability remains uncertain. Using monthly resolved Xisha coral Sr/Ca-SST and three hydroclimate reconstructions analyzed at native temporal resolution, we find that the Medieval Climate Anomaly (MCA, 1149–1205 CE) is the only sampled interval with a cross-proxy-consistent positive relationship. The annually resolved Zheng record remains positive after detrending and autocorrelation correction (r = 0.476, padj = 0.043), whereas non-MCA relationships are predominantly negative or near zero. East Asian winter monsoon (EAWM)-related variability is largest during the MCA among the six intervals, yet its association with teleconnection strength is weak (r = 0.52, p = 0.29), arguing against a universal threshold. Independent central-Pacific coral evidence indicates altered tropical-Pacific variability. Because winter-to-summer SST memory persists, we interpret the MCA reversal as downstream atmospheric reorganization, with EAWM variability as a possible preconditioning factor.

title: How different are tropical cyclone precipitation and convective properties during the evolution of fast-growing and slow-growing episodes
abstract:
How different are tropical cyclone precipitation and convective properties during the evolution of fast-growing and slow-growing episodes 
 Analyzing a 16-yr Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) satellite microwave imager (TMI) data for global tropical cyclones (TCs), this study examines the differences of various precipitation and convective properties in the TC’s inner core, specifically precipitation and convective intensity, symmetry, and frequency of various precipitation and convection types, during fast-growing (FG) versus slow-growing (SG) episodes. Instead of defining FG/SG as a 24-h period and treat each 24-h period as a separate case as in most previous statistical FG/SG studies, this work adopts an episode-based definition by consolidating all the continuous and overlapping 24-h FG/SG cases in each TC into FG/SG episodes to examine the evolution of each episode and compare the corresponding episode-relative stages between FG/SG episodes. The results show that FG episodes have significantly heavier rain rate, stronger convective intensities, more symmetric distribution of rain rate and convective intensity in the inner core for almost all corresponding episode-relative stages, compared with SG episodes. At the before-episode stage, FG episodes feature 11% heavier rain rate, 1% stronger convective intensity, 19% more stratiform rainfall frequency, 15% more shallow convection, 50% more deep convection, 21% more symmetric distribution of convective intensity, and 5% more asymmetric distribution of stratiform rainfall. These results can be used to improve FG predictions.

title: Turbulent mixing by non-breaking surface waves in the ocean: theory, observation and modeling
abstract:
Turbulent mixing by non-breaking surface waves in the ocean: theory, observation and modeling 
 Most ocean general-circulation models face the persistent challenge that the simulated summer ocean mixed layers are too shallow, indicating a lack of mixing; climate models coupled to them simulate too hot sea-surface temperatures (SSTs). Global wind energy input to the oceans supplies a great amount of energy to the surface waves. It is commonly thought that wave-induced turbulence mixing occurs only through wave breaking, but that turbulence, though intense, is injected only to a depth of the order of a wave height. Here we lay the theoretical foundation that non-breaking ocean surface waves can enhance background turbulence and increase irreversible mixing. Such turbulence dissipation and mixing extend to about a horizontal wavelength in depth, comparable to the mixed-layer depth. The direct wave-to-turbulence transfer of energy occurs without needing to be linked to the second-order Stokes drift, and mixing is thus more effective. When introduced into ocean models, such mixing effectively reduces model biases, producing deeper summer mixed layers and cooler SSTs where waves are stronger, as in observations. The predicted wave-turbulence interactions have characteristics which are consistent with laboratory and field observations, including the wave-modulation of turbulence as an energy transfer mechanism, and absence of phase locking to the wave.

title: Contribution of chemical components to cloud condensation nuclei prediction across multiple continental sites
abstract:
Contribution of chemical components to cloud condensation nuclei prediction across multiple continental sites 
 Aerosol–cloud interactions represent a major uncertainty in climate projections. Cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) are particles upon which cloud droplets form, yet in situ CCN measurements remain scarce. Aerosol chemical component exerts important control over CCN activity. It remains unclear how reliably aerosol chemical composition predicts CCN number concentration (NCCN). This study compiled a dataset of NCCN (supersaturation of 0.1 to 1%) collocated with aerosol chemical components at 20 global continental sites, spanning from remote natural to heavily polluted regions. This dataset was applied to evaluate global NCCN retrieval products from spaceborne Cloud Aerosol Lidar with Orthogonal Polarization (CALIOP) and Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), and to develop a chemical component-based random forest (RF) framework for NCCN prediction and key predictor identification at single-site, site-type, and unified spatial scales. CALIOP showed total normalized mean bias (NMB) of 33.6 ± 79.4% at 0.2% supersaturation (Pearson’s r of 0.72), and CAMS showed –33.6 ± 61.5% to 48.6 ± 79.7% across 0.1 − 1.0% supersaturation (Pearson’s r of 0.29 to 0.60). Three RF modeling scales produced an overall Pearson’s r of 0.80–0.85 and total NMB of −17.3 ± 20.9% to 0.1 ± 49.6% across 0.1–1% supersaturation over the compiled dataset, confirming the feasibility of this framework for NCCN prediction. Interpretability analysis identified inorganic species (ammonium at anthropogenic sites and sulfate at natural sites) as leading predictors at 0.1% supersaturation, whereas organic matter becomes dominant for higher supersaturation. Future work incorporating more observational datasets across diverse environments is expected to further improve the accuracy and generalizability of NCCN predictions.

title: Abrupt permafrost thaw overwhelms vegetation-driven erosion reduction in sediment export on the Tibetan Plateau
abstract:
Abrupt permafrost degradation through retrogressive thaw slumps can increase sediment delivery to Tibetan rivers, outweighing the greening-induced reduction in sediment export, suggests a study combining multi-decadal satellite observations, topographic differencing, and hydrological modelling. 
 Vegetation greening and abrupt permafrost thaw are reshaping sediment dynamics across the Tibetan Plateau, yet their relative effects on sediment delivery remain poorly quantified. Here we show that retrogressive thaw slumps are disproportionately important sediment sources, with erosion rates two to three orders of magnitude above undisturbed landscapes and source-to-channel connectivity generally exceeding 60%. Combining multi-decadal satellite observations, high-resolution topographic differencing and cold-region hydrological modelling, we quantify the competing effects of thaw-slump sediment supply and greening-induced erosion reduction. During 2000–2022, thaw slumps delivered more than four times as much non-ice sediment to channels as was reduced by greening, compensating for declining glacier-derived sediment and contributing to increased downstream suspended sediment export. Across permafrost regions, approximately 1.2‰ thaw-slump coverage represents an upper-bound threshold above which thaw-slump sediment delivery exceeds greening-induced sediment reduction. These results show that spatially limited abrupt thaw can outweigh widespread vegetation recovery in regulating sediment delivery from warming permafrost landscapes. title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response
abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)–associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealedMfn2up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. ElevatedMFN2expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown ofMfn2restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry–based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression onMfn2. Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocyticMfn2knockdown orStat1overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2–STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

title: Cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis regulates mast cell function
abstract: Steroid hormones are well-known regulators of mast cell function, but whether mast cells themselves produce steroids de novo and influences their effector function has remained unknown. Here, we show that mast cells constitutively express the steroidogenic enzyme cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member 1 (Cyp11a1) and produce pregnenolone. Cyp11a1 expression was detected across tissue-resident mast cells from multiple organs, was conserved in human mast cells, and was enhanced by interleukin-3 signaling and after activation. We identified Cyp11a1 as a Gata2-dependent, superenhancer-associated mast cell gene, placing steroidogenesis within the core mast cell transcriptional program. Loss of Cyp11a1 altered transcriptomic and proteomic programs in mast cells, with effects on pathways linked to cell growth, immune signaling, and effector function. Functionally, Cyp11a1-deficient mast cells showed increased degranulation in response to both immunoglobulin E (IgE)–dependent and IgE-independent stimulation. In vivo, loss of Cyp11a1 reduced mast cell abundance in several tissues but exacerbated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis. These findings identify cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis as a regulatory pathway that restrains mast cell activation and anaphylactic responses.

title: Kinetic-driven microphase separation and vitrification of crowded hydrogels with associative bonds
abstract: The thermal response of stimuli-responsive hydrogels is typically viewed through thermodynamic equilibrium. However, in “crowded” networks with dense associative bonds, elasticity and diffusion kinetics dictate distinct nonequilibrium fates. We investigate thermal transitions of a PAAc-CaAc2(polyacrylic acid complexed with calcium ions) hydrogel along two trajectories: a quasi-static isobaric pathway (path A) and a rapid quasi-isochoric pathway (path B). Along path A, the gel contracts homogeneously until reaching a hardening temperature via global vitrification (Thard). In contrast, path B triggers confined microphase separation into polymer-dense and dilute phases at a critical temperature (Tdem), followed by a hardening transition via localized vitrification (ThardPS). We demonstrate thatTdemis governed by a mechanical-thermodynamic competition: The internal pressure (Pc) to trigger demixing scales linearly with the permanent-network shear modulus (Gx), maintaining a ratio ofPc/Gx≈ 100. We identifyThardandThardPSas distinct hardening points, with elastically constrained local water content governingThardPS. This framework provides a strategy for programming nonequilibrium fates and “lockable” properties of responsive soft matter.

title: Peripheral nerve injury alters metabolic function and neuronal excitability through the Lin28/let-7 pathway
abstract: Sensory neurons require efficient metabolic processes to reliably transmit information including touch, temperature, and noxious stimuli from peripheral to central nervous systems. Peripheral nerve injury is known to disrupt metabolic function resulting in aberrant sensory nervous system excitation, but molecular pathways linking nerve injury to persistent alterations in metabolism and neuronal activity have been incompletely understood. We find that a conserved metabolic regulator, RNA binding protein Lin28, is elevated in the somas of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) nociceptive neurons following nerve injury but exhibits a higher and more enduring local induction in peripheral sensory axons of the injured nerve. Growth suppressor let-7 family microRNAs (miRNAs), whose biogenesis is inhibited by Lin28, are down-regulated following injury, consistent with the spatiotemporal course of Lin28 induction. Genome-wide sensory neuron-specific and nociceptor-enriched profiling of miRNA:target RNA interactions reveals abundant let-7 miRNA targeting of metabolic transcripts in healthy sensory axons, which is diminished by nerve injury. Consistently, injured sciatic nerves exhibit disrupted cellular respiration near the site of nerve injury, which is alleviated by local restoration of let-7 miRNAs. Selective Lin28 knockout in nociceptive sensory neurons also alleviates the metabolic disturbances of nerve injury as well as suppressing injury-induced elevation of activity in ipsilateral peripheral sensory neurons and central spinal cord dorsal horn neurons. These results implicate the Lin28/let-7 pathway as a critical driver of metabolic dysregulation and the pathophysiology of heightened sensory nervous system activity following nerve injury.

title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate–activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor–associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2T175Amutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation
abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion ofFbn1in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor–β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix–mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.
